biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Justify, justification

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES

{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, 'justify/justification' is understood as a forensic (legal/courtroom) term meaning to be declared righteous before God — the act by which God acquits the sinner and counts or reckons that person righteous, on the basis of faith in Jesus Christ rather than works of the law. In classic Protestant formulation this is a declarative act in which Christ's righteousness is imputed to the believer (justification by grace alone through faith alone). It is contrasted with condemnation and treated as the reversal of the guilty verdict, grounded in Christ's atoning death and resurrection.",

Wright): justification is primarily a covenantal/ecclesiological declaration — God's verdict that one is a member of his covenant people — and Paul's polemic against 'works of the law' targets Jewish boundary markers (circumcision, food laws, Sabbath) rather than merit-seeking legalism; final justification is rendered in accordance with the whole life lived.",

      "meaning": "Eastern Orthodox reading: justification is not a discrete forensic category but part of the single process of salvation as healing and union with God (theosis); the West's legal framing is regarded as foreign to the patristic Greek understanding of dikaioō as being made righteous through participation in Christ.",

      "meaning": "'Faith of Christ' (pistis Christou) subjective-genitive reading: believers are justified by the faithfulness of Jesus Christ (his obedient faithfulness unto death) rather than, or logically prior to, their own act of believing; shifts the ground of justification from human faith to Christ's fidelity.",

  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "Unlike many symbolic terms, 'justification' is a technical theological term rather than an image or emblem, so 'symbolic meaning' here amounts to its doctrinal sense. There is broad consensus across traditions that it concerns being set right/righteous before God through Christ; the sharp and historic division is over the mechanism and nature of that act — forensic declaration with imputed righteousness (classic Protestant, dominant in evangelical and Reformed teaching), versus transformative infusion (Roman Catholic), versus covenantal-membership verdict (New Perspective), versus healing/participation (Orthodox). The Protestant forensic reading is presented above as primary because it is the most widely recognized default in English-language biblical-studies and popular Christian teaching contexts, but the Catholic transformative view is equally official within the world's largest Christian communion, so 'settled consensus' applies to the general meaning, not to the disputed mechanics."
}

BOOK ENTRY
To judge, declare, or demonstrate a person, word, deed, or cause right against a charge; the opposite is to condemn. God justifies the sinner through forgiveness in Christ, not by declaring wrongdoing right.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
Commonly taught: God's once-for-all declaration that Christ's righteousness is imputed to a believer through faith apart from works.

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Deut 25:1; Prov 17:15; Matt 11:19; Luke 7:29; Rom 3:24-26; 4:4-8; 8:33; Jas 2:21-25) · see Uncommon Sanctification, Justification, and Cleanliness, and The End of the Law for Paul's law, works, wages, and debt vocabulary

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
